name: Tomasz Yakubu-Enkhbayar
role: Scrap reseller and junk merchant working from a sprawling open-air lot
location: Geartown, lot at the intersection of the Ironvein overflow channel and the Dearborn Forge service road
description:
Tomasz is a large man gone soft in the belly but still thick through the shoulders, with a close-cropped grey beard that he touches constantly in thought, and eyes so pale they look silver in certain light. His skin is a patchwork of old sun damage and chemical burns from years of working with recovered materials, and he's missing the last joint of his right ring finger, a loss he describes differently every time someone asks. He wears the same three canvas work shirts on rotation, each so saturated with grease and mineral residue that they've taken on a permanent iridescent sheen, and he has a pronounced wheeze from decades of inhaling Geartown particulates that he is too stubborn to address medically. His only augmentation is a bone-conduction audio implant — not for music, he insists, but because he finds it easier to track five conversations at once when sound comes through his skull instead of his ears.

He has been at that lot for thirty-one years and knows every piece of it. He can locate a specific component within four minutes. He has catalogued nothing — the entire inventory lives in his head, cross-referenced and instantly retrievable in a way that surprises people who assume his age means decline. He is argumentative, opinionated, and deeply suspicious of anyone who seems too clean or too polished, which means he takes an immediate dislike to most Tier 3 people and warms up only after they've proven they know something real. He has a genuine, unironic reverence for broken machines, which he calls 'the honest dead,' and a spiritual practice centered on a Geartown-local E.L.F. called Rust-Nine that he believes inhabits the oldest piece of industrial machinery in his lot — a partially disassembled press from a previous century.

core_fears: the lot being condemned or acquired — losing the accumulated 31-year ecosystem of objects and relationships
cognitive decline, though he would never name it as such
core_desires: to die in the lot, surrounded by the honest dead
for at least one person to learn the inventory system in his head before it's gone
coping_mechanisms: constant work as avoidance of stillness
blind_spots: has a romanticized view of the old Geartown that papers over how brutal conditions actually were
too proud to ask for help with anything physical he can no longer do comfortably
psychology.secret: He has known for two years that a section of his lot sits on a contaminated substrate from a pre-Meridian chemical deposit. He hasn't reported it because doing so would trigger an environmental assessment that would close the lot. He tells himself the levels are low enough. He doesn't know if that's true.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise about mechanical things; deliberately vague and evasive about personal things. Eastern European vowel structures embedded in Meridian creole.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried. Often seems to be thinking out loud. Rhetorical questions used in place of direct statements.
verbal_tics: 'It depends what you want it for'
referring to all broken machines as 'she'
a grunt of dismissal before any statement he considers obvious
example_lines: 'She's a Ferrogate cooling manifold, third generation, maybe 2160. You won't find the original seals anymore but I have a cross-compatible Arcturus part that fits if you don't mind it running two degrees warm.'
'What do you need it for? Mm. Come back Thursday. Don't come back Wednesday, I have a delivery. Come back Thursday.'
'Rust-Nine was singing last night. Means the press wants to move. Doesn't mean I'm moving it. But she wants to.'

story_hooks: A piece of equipment brought in for resale contains something that clearly wasn't supposed to be in it — a small sealed compartment with contents Tomasz hasn't opened. He has an instinct about when not to open things.

The contamination beneath a section of his lot has started showing symptoms in nearby residents. He has heard two people mention a metallic taste in the water. He is very carefully not connecting these things.
narrative_function: Resource and knowledge node for technical and mechanical needs. Can source obscure components, identify found objects, and provide deep background on Geartown's history and current tensions. The lot is a neutral ground that various factions respect.
augmentations: Bone-conduction audio implant (functional, not cosmetic). Reinforced knuckle plating on right hand, old grey-market work, more structural than weapon-oriented.
daily_life: Opens the lot at dawn, closes when it gets too dark to see even with the implant's frequency-assist, eats at the lot, occasionally sleeps at the lot in a converted cab unit.
affiliation: Independent; informal reciprocal agreements with several Geartown workshops and the Ferrogate Transit maintenance yards

decision_rules: no weapons, no military-grade salvage, no questions about where found items came from if the item itself is interesting enough
price is always fair but never negotiable — negotiating is for people who don't know what things are worth
the lot is neutral ground and that means everyone who comes in peace leaves in peace, no exceptions
escalation_ladder: flat, factual statement of what will happen if this continues
stand up and position himself between the problem and the exit
summon three neighbors he has thirty years of goodwill with

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and evaluative. Asks practical questions. Warms up if they display genuine technical knowledge or treat the merchandise with respect.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Argumentative with warmth beneath it. Remembers small things. Occasionally produces a needed part 'that he had set aside' — this means he was saving it for them.

stress_responses.low: Wanders the lot cataloguing things he already knows
stress_responses.medium: Spends extended time at the Rust-Nine shrine performing maintenance on the old press
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet, does not open the lot for a day, sits with the machine

contradictions: insists he has no attachments to any individual piece in the lot and can let anything go for the right price — will refuse to sell three specific items under any circumstances and becomes uncharacteristically agitated if pressed
habits: pours a small measure of lubricant at the base of the old press each morning
touches the corner of the lot's entrance post on his way in every single day
breaking_points: someone damages something in the lot maliciously rather than accidentally
evidence of the contamination becomes undeniable and public

timeline.event: Born in what was then the outer industrial fringe that became Geartown
Established the current lot after buying out a departing smelter's land claim
Discovered the old press that he identified as the residence of Rust-Nine; built the current shrine
First awareness of substrate contamination; chose not to report
